One fix to the streaming transport, reported by a consumer: a subscription disposed as the connection dropped could throw from `DisposeAsync`. Nothing else moves. **90 of IBKR's 108 Trading endpoints, plus the socket**, as in `v0.4.0-preview.1`.

```sh
dotnet add package IbkrDotNet.Extensions.DependencyInjection --prerelease
```

## What is fixed

`IIbkrStreamingTransport.SendAsync` reports a lost connection as `IbkrStreamingException`, whatever the socket did, so that a consumer handles a lost line in one place. One shape escaped: a frame waiting its turn behind another send when the connection dropped came back as `TaskCanceledException` from the send gate, where the same loss a few microseconds later, inside the send, was an `IbkrStreamingException`. `StreamingSubscription.DisposeAsync` sends `umd` through that path and catches only the streaming exception, so a subscription disposed while the socket was going away, in the `finally` its documentation asks for, could throw ([#62](https://github.com/jerbersoft/ibkrdotnet/issues/62)).

The wait for the gate now sits inside the same handling as the send, and a cancellation out of `SendAsync` can only be the caller's own. Winning the gate is checked against the connection as well: the runtime can grant a wait whose token was already cancelled when a release lands first, and the first CI run of the fix caught a frame reaching the socket that way, after the connection had been torn down. Nothing goes out on a line that is gone.

`StreamingSubscription`'s remarks now say what the `finally` advice assumed: disposing does not throw when the socket has gone. The unsubscribe frame is logged as unsent, at debug, and IBKR released the market data line with the connection. A consumer that catches `OperationCanceledException` around `DisposeAsync` as a workaround can drop it.

## Nothing else changed

No public signature moved; the API transcript is identical to `v0.4.0-preview.1`. The scripted `WebSocket` the tests drive can now hold a send open, which is how the scenario is reproduced without timing: the held send and the queued `umd` are each provably where the test needs them before the socket drops. 554 tests, three of them new.

## Why this is still a prerelease

For the reason `v0.4.0-preview.1` gave. The socket has been driven end to end over a scripted `WebSocket` and not yet against a live gateway; [#60](https://github.com/jerbersoft/ibkrdotnet/issues/60) tracks that run and the `.live.json` capture.

## Publishing

Pushed by [Trusted Publishing](https://learn.microsoft.com/nuget/nuget-org/trusted-publishing) over OIDC, as the previous two versions were; both packages are also attached to this release.
